verdicts.originEvidence: git diff 8ecb878f HEAD over swatch-tool.ts, config-controller.ts, config-sidebar.ts, tool-config-types.ts is empty; 8ecb878f:tool-config-types.ts:489-491 has the hairColors/SeekerOfTheSun/Female defaults
verdicts.repro: Fresh profile, Swatch on Eye palette: change max results or a display option in the sidebar -> controller.setConfig notifies the full config -> palette switches to Hair, tribe to Seeker/Female, selection nulled, all persisted
verdicts.evidence:
config-controller.ts:306-334 merges and notifies the full config; config-sidebar.ts:813/873/907 write partials; tool-config-types.ts:489 vs swatch-tool.ts:158-163 defaults
Only writers of colorSheet: swatch-tool.ts:1587/1796/1825 call the tool-local setConfig; subscribe (config-controller.ts:346) does not fire on subscribe, so the flip happens on the next notification
verdicts.fix: Make ConfigController the single owner: seed subrace/gender/colorSheet/maxResults from getConfig('swatch'), route rail/slot picks through ConfigController.setConfig('swatch', {colorSheet}), align the default table with the tool (web-app deploy only)
verdicts.reason: Every hop is traced. The sidebar writes a partial, the controller merges it into stored or default values and broadcasts the whole object, and swatch setConfig treats colorSheet/race/gender as authoritative. Nothing ever writes the tool's colorSheet into the controller.

skeptic.reason: I traced the path from the code and reproduced it with a real ConfigController; the finding holds. On a fresh profile the tool starts from its own DEFAULTS: eyeColors, Midlander, Male (swatch-tool.ts:158-163, 309-331). The controller starts from different defaults: hairColors, SeekerOfTheSun, Female (tool-config-types.ts:488-491). onMount (swatch-tool.ts:360-408) never seeds the tool from getConfig('swatch'). The palette rail, range toggle and slot pick call only the tool's own setConfig (swatch-tool.ts:1587, 1796, 1825), so the controller's colorSheet is never written. On the other side, the sidebar's handleConfigChange (config-sidebar.ts:813) and its display-option and dye-filter fan-outs (873, 907) send partial updates. ConfigController.setConfig (config-controller.ts:306-334) merges each partial into the stored or default config and broadcasts the whole object. The swatch subscriber (swatch-tool.ts:376) passes that object to setConfig, and setConfig treats colorSheet, race and gender as authoritative (450-472). It reloads the colors, sets selectedColor to null and persists everything to the tool's storage keys. No other guard sits on the path: v4-layout's config-change forward only adds a harmless partial, and pinToCharaFile pins only race and gender. Because the rail still never writes to the controller, the flip comes back on every later sidebar change. Existing tests miss it because swatch-tool.test.ts mocks ConfigController with a subscribe that never fires. Severity stays HIGH. Changing max results, a display option, the matching method or a dye filter while on Swatch is an ordinary action, and it silently switches the palette and tribe/gender and drops the selection. The user can recover by clicking the Eye chip, but the next setting change flips it again.
skeptic.evidence:

It used the real ConfigController after localStorage.clear(), subscribed SwatchTool.prototype.setConfig bound to a fake tool state {colorCategory:'eyeColors', subrace:'Midlander', gender:'Male', selectedColor:{...}}, then called cc.setConfig('swatch', {maxResults:5}). The test passed, asserting colorCategory === 'hairColors', subrace === 'SeekerOfTheSun', gender === 'Female' and selectedColor === null. Key lines: config-controller.ts:311-334 (merge, then notifyListeners with the full newConfig); swatch-tool.ts:466 `if (config.colorSheet !== undefined && config.colorSheet !== this.colorCategory)`; tool-config-types.ts:489 `colorSheet: 'hairColors'` vs swatch-tool.ts:161 `colorCategory: 'eyeColors'`. A git grep finds no setConfig('swatch', ...) call outside config-sidebar.ts and config-controller.ts:204.

skeptic.evidence:
Paths are under /c/dev/XIVProjects/xivdyetools/.claude/worktrees/preview-2026-10-04/apps/web-app/src.

- **The update path.** harmony-tool.ts:311-316 subscribes `LanguageService.subscribe(() => this.update())` in onMount. base-component.ts:148-160 has update() call unbindAllEvents, then render() (which runs renderContent()), then bindEvents(), then `this.onUpdate?.()`.

Its method list has none, and a grep for `onUpdate` across components/*-tool.ts matches only gradient-tool.ts:466. That method exists to fix this same problem in GradientTool ("update() rebuilds both panels (e.g. on language change) — repopulate").
- **The empty grid.** renderContent (harmony-tool.ts:259-272) runs destroyChildComponents, then renderLeftPanel and renderRightPanel. renderRightPanel clears rightPanel and creates a new empty `harmonyGridContainer` (harmony-tool.ts:1119-1122). It also creates `emptyStateContainer` with class 'hidden' (harmony-tool.ts:1127-1130) and never calls showEmptyState, so neither results nor the empty state are visible. The Share button gets `disabled = !this.selectedDye`, which is false when a dye is selected (harmony-tool.ts:1106).
- **Nothing calls generateHarmonies() on this path.** I checked every call site (lines 398, 410, 420, 608, 619, 824, 854, 857, 973, 1020, 1364, 1690, 1943, 2001, 2031). Each one is driven by user input, config, routing or mount, never by a language change.
- **The rebuilt DyeSelector.** buildBaseDyePanel (harmony-tool.ts:697-698) calls `selector.setSelectedDyes([this.selectedDye])`. dye-selector.ts:486-489 only assigns and calls update(), with no emit. DyeSelector emits selection-changed only on clear-all, escape, pick and remove (dye-selector.ts:195, 206, 285, 375).
- **Listeners added during the notification.** language-service.ts:116 iterates a Set with forEach, so the subscribers that the new DyeSelector and MarketBoard add mid-iteration do run. Both only call update(). MarketBoard emits server-changed / showPricesChanged only on user or service events (market-board.ts:300, 319, 455, 482, 544, 566), not on update().
- **The app shell.** v4-layout.ts:338-342 only refreshes the document title on a language change. It does not remount the tool.
- **No test covers it.** harmony-tool.test.ts mocks `LanguageService.subscribe` as a no-op (lines 99, 127), so no test fires a language change.
- **No repro test run.** I did not run a repro test. A `__repro__skeptic.test.ts` from another session, which tests SwatchTool, already sits in components/__tests__, and I left it alone to avoid a collision. The static path above is complete and deterministic.
- **Severity.** Brief scale: a wrong result on an edge path, so MEDIUM. Not LOW, because the user loses the results entirely rather than seeing a cosmetic glitch. Not HIGH, because a language switch is infrequent and any dye or type interaction restores the results.
- **Origin.** MAIN.

verdicts.title: budget-tool.ts findAlternatives has no run guard; a superseded run overwrites this.rows after a newer run

A superseded fetch returns an empty Map (market-board-service.ts:359-365), but the continuation still writes this.rows (582-598) and renders. Reordering needs two overlapping uncached batches with different keys, such as the mount fetch plus an early slider tick or selectDye. After the first fetch the consolidated IDs come from cache. Edge path, hence MEDIUM.

skeptic.reason:
The race is real, but it is narrower than the finding says. budget-tool.ts:546-606 reads the target and threshold before `await this.fetchPrices` (577) and writes `this.rows` (582-598) afterwards with no generation check. A superseded call still returns normally with an empty Map (market-board-service.ts:359-365), so the stale continuation runs to the end and renders. renderLedger (1393-1435) draws whatever `this.rows` holds under the current `this.targetDye`.

What limits it: cofferDyes() (530-532) always adds all 20 non-consolidated dyes, and custom dyes have a negative itemID, so they are filtered out by shouldFetchPrice (296-301). Each run's market-ID set is therefore those 20 plus whichever of the consolidated IDs 52254/52255/52256 its target and candidates touch. When two runs ask for the same uncached set, APIService.ts:987-1005 shares one promise between them. Both resume in start order, so the newer run writes last and the stale write is never painted.

The reorder only happens when the two runs differ in which consolidated types they touch, or when one run is fully cached and the other is not. Cache writes are synchronous, because the wrapper's `set` updates memory and does not wait for IndexedDB, so no other timing window opens there.

Concrete cases:
- **Mount:** the mount run without a target fetches 20 IDs. An early selectDye of a Type-A dye fetches 21. If the second request returns first, the late mount run captured `target = null` and sets `this.rows = []`, so the new target shows an empty ledger.
- **Two quick picks:** pick T1 (Type C, not yet cached), then quickly T2 (types already cached). T2 resolves almost at once, and T1's late continuation writes T1's rows under T2's card.

The 5-minute API_CACHE_TTL re-opens this window during a long session. No test covers superseded runs (budget-tool.test.ts has no race or superseded case). It needs out-of-order completion or a cache-state change within network latency, so it is an edge path, but the result is a visibly wrong ledger. That fits MEDIUM, not LOW.
skeptic.evidence:

- budget-tool.ts:530-532: `cofferDyes()` returns every non-consolidated dye with itemID > 0, so the batch key changes only with the consolidated types a run touches.
- apps/web-app/src/services/market-board-service.ts:359-365: the superseded path returns `new Map()` instead of throwing, and fetchPrices (625-647) swallows that.
- packages/core/src/services/APIService.ts:987-1005: only identical uncached sets share a batch.
- api-service-wrapper.ts:96-102: `set` is synchronous in memory, so there is no write-window race.
- custom-dye.ts:41-44: custom dyes get a negative itemID and are excluded.
- packages/core/src/constants/index.ts:134: API_CACHE_TTL is 5 minutes.
- budget-tool.test.ts has no superseded or race test.
- No repro test file was written.

skeptic.reason:
The defect is real, and I could not refute it. I re-traced it in the code without using the finding's description:
- The in-page slider handler (budget-tool.ts:991-998) only sets this.matchLine, writes STORAGE_KEYS.matchLine and calls findAlternatives. It never calls ConfigController, so the stored budget.maxDeltaE stays at its default of 8 (tool-config-types.ts:483).
- A sidebar display-option toggle then runs config-sidebar.ts:838-873, which calls setConfig('budget', { displayOptions }). Dye filters go the same way through :893-907.
- ConfigController.setConfig (config-controller.ts:306-334) merges the change into the stored config. The OPT-008 no-op skip does not fire because displayOptions really changed, so it notifies the full config, including maxDeltaE 8.
- BudgetTool.setConfig (:328-342) then computes clampMatchLine(8) = 8, which differs from 14. It overwrites matchLine, persists 8 and re-runs the search.
- In the display-options and dye-filter cases nothing re-renders the slider, so its thumb stays at 14 while the value label shows 8. In the matching-method case renderMain re-renders it at 8, but the user's 14 is still lost.

No guard prevents this: v4-layout.ts:189-192 forwards only the single changed key, but the subscription path above still delivers the full config. No test catches it. budget-tool.test.ts never fires the slider's input event. The e2e test at budget-tool.spec.ts:120-124 only sets the slider and never checks it after a sidebar change.

MEDIUM is right rather than HIGH, because this is a two-step path that is easy to recover from:
- The user has to use the in-page slider instead of the sidebar one, then change another sidebar setting while still on the Budget tool.
- Re-dragging the slider fixes it.
- No data is lost.

It is not LOW either. The ledger silently changes which dyes count as matches, and the slider then shows a value that no longer matches the results.
skeptic.evidence:
The slider handler in apps/web-app/src/components/budget-tool.ts:991-998 has no ConfigController call:
`this.on(slider, 'input', () => { this.matchLine = parseInt(slider.value, 10); ... StorageService.setItem(STORAGE_KEYS.matchLine, this.matchLine); void this.findAlternatives(); });`

Each step of the reset, with the file it is in:
1. A display-option toggle fans out per tool: config-sidebar.ts:873 calls `setConfig(tool, { displayOptions: allOptions })`, and budget is one of those tools.
2. config-controller.ts:311-334 builds `newConfig = {...currentConfig, ...partial}`, which carries the stored maxDeltaE of 8, then calls `notifyListeners(key, newConfig)`.

verdicts.title: budget-tool.ts saveSwapRecord breaks 216-gil ties by database order, not by ΔE
verdicts.reason: priceOf gives every tier-A row gil = CONSOLIDATED_DYES.A.price (216). The reduce uses strict < over this.rows, which is in getAllDyes order (582-598, unsorted), so the first Standard dye in range is saved, not the closest. Save swap is live (renderTargetOverview:1191). MEDIUM: an edge feature.

verdicts.fix: Tie-break lexicographically on (gil, de), or pick the best perPoint row. Web-app only.

skeptic.reason:
The mechanism is real. In apps/web-app/src/components/budget-tool.ts, priceOf (lines 478-480) prices every tier-A dye at CONSOLIDATED_DYES.A.price. The saveSwapRecord reduce (lines 1229-1237) keeps only rows with a strictly lower gil. this.rows is built in getAllDyes order and is never sorted (lines 582-598). So when several tier-A rows tie at 216, the first one in database order is saved, not the closest by ΔE. The ledger's default perPoint sort (lines 670-676) puts the closest 216-gil dye at the top, so the saved dye can differ from the row the user sees first. No test covers saveSwapRecord.

I would grade it LOW, not MEDIUM. The saved dye is still at the minimum price and still inside the match line the user picked, so it is an acceptable substitute by the user's own rule. That matches the method's docstring ("best-priced substitute") literally. The defect is a weak tie-break inside an optional, device-local "Save swap" record: nothing is lost, the main ledger and verdict are correct, and the user can see the closer option in the ledger. That makes it closer to cosmetic or suboptimal than a wrong result.
skeptic.evidence: budget-tool.ts:478-480 `if (tier === 'A') return { tier, gil: meta.price, ... }`; :1229-1237 `(best?.price.gil == null || r.price.gil < best.price.gil) ? r : best` (strict <, so the first row wins a tie); :582-598 rows = candidates.map(...).filter(...) with no sort, and candidates come from dyeService.getAllDyes() order (:556); :1191 the Save swap button is live on the target card for any real dye; sortRows :670-676 ranks by perPoint and then de, so the ledger's top 216-gil row is the closest one; git grep finds no test that calls saveSwapRecord (only collection-service tests create swap records directly). After a share link or an 'Inspect in Harmony' hand-off puts ?dye=X in the URL, a base dye the user then picks only reaches storage; nothing rewrites the URL, and every tool switch carries dye= forward. skeptic.reason: I could not refute it. I re-derived the path from the code and the defect happens as described, so MEDIUM stands. A language switch while dyes are selected leaves the right panel showing the empty state. Export/Share and the duel stay hidden until the next add or remove, but the selection itself is kept. Each switch also leaks a full set of live left-panel components. The origin is MAIN, and no unit or e2e test switches language in this tool.
skeptic.evidence:
Path walked (origin MAIN: `git diff --stat 8ecb878f HEAD` over comparison-tool.ts, base-component.ts and v4-layout.ts is empty):
1. **The language listener.** language-modal.ts:201 calls `LanguageService.setLocale`. At language-service.ts:116 that loops over a Set of listeners. comparison-tool.ts:229 is subscribed and calls `this.update()`. v4-layout.ts:338 only refreshes the tab title, so the shell never reloads the tool.
2. **The re-render.** `update()` (base-component.ts:148-163) runs unbindAllEvents, then render, then `safeRender()` and `renderContent()`, then bindEvents and `onUpdate?.()`. ComparisonTool has no `onUpdate`.
3. **renderContent (comparison-tool.ts:211-220).** It calls `renderLeftPanel()` and then `renderRightPanel()`. It never calls `updateResults()`.
4. **The right panel (comparison-tool.ts:842-965).** It is rebuilt from scratch:
   - `emptyStateContainer` has no inline display, so it is visible.
   - `actionsRow` (Export/Share) is created with `display: none` (line 871).
   - `selectedDyesSection`, `pairChipsSection` and `duelSection` are all created with `display: none` (lines 902, 928, 957).
5. **Visibility.** Only `updateResults()` (1140-1173) and `showEmptyState()` (2025-2041) change these display values. Neither runs during the language update.
6. **No later caller.** `setConfig` only re-renders on a ConfigController emit. config-sidebar.ts:692 reacts to a language change with `requestUpdate` only.

Result: with 2-4 dyes, the empty-state "select at least two dyes" message and the placeholder slots show, and the duel and Export/Share are hidden. `this.selectedDyes` and the persisted list are untouched, so the next add/remove or a reload recovers.

The "dyes dropped" consequence is correctly ruled out. DyeSelector's own language listener (dye-selector.ts:477-478) only calls `update()`, and no `selection-changed` is emitted on that path (that event fires only at lines 195, 206, 285 and 375, all user-driven). In V4, leftPanel and rightPanel are the same element (v4-layout.ts:636-640), so the new selector is detached anyway.

The leak is real. `renderLeftPanel` (452-526) overwrites `dyeSelector`, the three CollapsiblePanels and `marketBoard` without destroying the old ones. The old DyeSelector and MarketBoard keep their LanguageService and favorites subscriptions (dye-selector.ts:468, 477; market-board.ts:437). Each old DyeSelector also re-binds a document `keydown` listener on every later language change (dye-selector.ts:246). `destroy()` only tears down the latest set, so the leaked sets survive navigation away from the tool. Contrast mixer-tool.ts:583-591, which skips `renderLeftPanel` in V4.

Tests: comparison-tool.test.ts only mocks LanguageService and never fires a locale change. No e2e comparison spec mentions language or locale.

Severity: a wrong, misleading result on an edge path (switching language mid-session with dyes loaded), with no data loss and recovery on the next interaction. That fits MEDIUM, not HIGH.

I did not write a repro test: an untracked `__repro__skeptic.test.ts` from another session already sits in apps/web-app/src/components/__tests__/, and the static path is unambiguous.

skeptic.reason: I couldn't refute this; the finding holds as described. A language switch makes onMount's language subscriber (accessibility-tool.ts:265-267) call BaseComponent.update() (base-component.ts:148-163). update() only re-renders and calls onUpdate, and AccessibilityTool defines no onUpdate. The re-render shows the empty state and hides the lens, pair and card sections even though dyes are still selected. It also drops any custom colour from a mixed selection. Nothing restores the results: v4-layout's language subscriber only refreshes the page title, config-sidebar only calls requestUpdate, and setConfig re-renders only when a value changed. No test covers update() or a language change. MEDIUM is right: a visible wrong result on an uncommon path. Selection ids stay in storage, and the results return on the next selection change.
skeptic.evidence:
Re-derived by reading the code; I did not run a repro test. An untracked __repro__skeptic.test.ts from another session already sits in the target directory, so writing my own would have collided with it.

1. Mount (apps/web-app/src/components/v4-layout.ts:621-631): the tool is created with leftPanel === rightPanel === mainPanel and drawerContent null. init() runs render, bindEvents, then onMount. The only call that fills the right panel at mount is onMount's updateResults() (accessibility-tool.ts:281-283).

2. Language change: the subscriber at accessibility-tool.ts:265-267 calls this.update(). base-component.ts:148-163 then runs unbindAllEvents, render (renderContent) and bindEvents. There is no updateResults call, and grep finds no onUpdate in accessibility-tool.ts.

3. renderContent (accessibility-tool.ts:247-256) calls renderRightPanel (726-932). That clears the panel and builds emptyStateContainer with inline display:flex (732-748). selectedDyesSection (759-761), lensSection (854-856) and pairSection (880-882) are each built with display:none. showEmptyState(false) is reached only through updateResults (1219-1233). Result: with 2 dyes and a lens selected, the add-dye empty state shows and the lens grid, pair readout and result cards stay hidden until the selection changes.

4. Custom colours: makeCustomDye (apps/web-app/src/shared/custom-dye.ts:40-44) gives each one a negative synthetic id. selectDye (accessibility-tool.ts:364-365) saves that id to storage along with the real ones. On re-render, renderDyeSelector (565-574) maps the saved ids through getAllDyes(), filters out ids it cannot find, and when at least one real dye resolves, assigns `this.selectedDyes = restoredDyes`. So for [dye, custom #FF8800], selectedDyes becomes [dye] and the custom colour is lost for the rest of the session.

5. Nothing else restores the results:
   - v4-layout.ts:338-342 only calls RouterService.refreshDocumentTitle().
   - v4/config-sidebar.ts:692-694 only calls requestUpdate().
   - setConfig (accessibility-tool.ts:449-470) calls updateResults only when needsRerender is true, which a language change does not set.

6. Tests: apps/web-app/src/components/__tests__/accessibility-tool.test.ts has no test that calls update() or switches language. Its mocked LanguageService.subscribe returns a no-op.

7. Origin: MAIN.

Mitigations, none of which lower the grade below MEDIUM: storage still holds the real dye ids, custom colours are documented as never persisting across sessions, and the next selection change restores the view.

verdicts.title: comparison-tool.ts buildSevenReadouts: the ΔE2000 tier skips tierFor's 0->1 bump, so it contradicts the verdict when matchThreshold < 5
verdicts.reason: tierFor (1190-1197) returns 0 only below matchThreshold and otherwise bumps a band tier of 0 to 1. The readout loop (1914-1915) takes classifyBandTier and forces 0 below the threshold, but never bumps. The ciede2000 match cuts are [5,10,20] (band-vocabulary.ts:94), and the sidebar slider allows 1-15 (config-sidebar.ts:1257-1260).
verdicts.repro: matchThreshold=2, active method ciede2000, pair ΔE2000=3.0 -> verdict and chips say CLOSE (tierFor=1), while the ΔE2000 readout row in the same duel says SAME (tier 0)

verdicts.originEvidence: git diff --stat 8ecb878f HEAD -- comparison-tool.ts is empty
verdicts.fix: Parameterise tierFor(value, method) and use it for the readout rows, so one function owns the SAME cut.

skeptic.reason: I could not refute it, and MEDIUM is the right grade. I worked it through by hand. tierFor (comparison-tool.ts:1190-1197) bumps a ciede2000 band tier of 0 up to 1 once the value is at or above matchThreshold. The readout loop (1912-1915) only forces 0 below the threshold and never bumps. With the match cuts at [5,10,20] and the slider allowing 1-15, any threshold below 5 leaves a gap between the threshold and 5 where the two disagree. In the same duel the verdict and chips say CLOSE while the ΔE2000 readout row says SAME, and the slider puts that pair above the SAME line. The default threshold is 5, so the user has to lower the slider first. That makes it a wrong result on an edge path, which is MEDIUM rather than HIGH. It is not just cosmetic, because the row contradicts the verdict next to it. Nothing tests it, and the code already exists on main.

- comparison-tool.ts:1914-1915: `let tier = classifyBandTier(value, method, 'match'); if (method === 'ciede2000' && value < this.matchThreshold) tier = 0;`. Nothing bumps tier 0 to 1 here.

skeptic.reason:
I could not refute this finding, and MEDIUM is the right severity. In config-sidebar.ts:669-701, connectedCallback subscribes only to 'swatch' and 'harmony'. Every other config value is copied once in loadConfigsFromController (:751-769). The sidebar stays mounted across tool switches: v4-layout-shell.ts:1019 removes it only for 'glamour', and the shell updates only the .activeTool property. So writes from outside the sidebar never reach its local copies:
- budget-tool.ts:292 calls setShowPrices(true), which writes market.showPrices at market-board-service.ts:251-256. The sidebar toggle at :2006 is bound to the stale this.marketConfig.showPrices.
- Settings reset (advanced-options-panel.ts:239-240) runs resetAllConfigs, which notifies each key (config-controller.ts:369-385). The 'settings-reset' event it dispatches has no listener anywhere.
- After a reset, flipping one display option re-sends the stale full set, which reverts the reset for every display option. display-options-v4.ts:325-334 emits getCurrentOptions(), built from its stale props. config-sidebar.ts:853-873 then writes that whole object to 'global' and to all 8 tools. setConfig merges it in (config-controller.ts:306-315).
No test covers this. config-sidebar.test.ts mocks subscribe, and the mixing-mode and wheel tests only check labels and the wheel. The cause is on main: git diff 8ecb878f..HEAD is empty for config-sidebar.ts, display-options-v4.ts, budget-tool.ts, config-controller.ts and advanced-options-panel.ts.
Why not higher or lower: the Budget case happens on a common path, but the effect is cosmetic. Prices do turn on, the toggle just shows off, and one click brings it back in line. The reset case is a real wrong result, because it silently undoes a destructive reset, but it is an edge path. That fits MEDIUM, not HIGH and not LOW.

skeptic.reason:
I could not refute it. dye-palette-drawer.ts:1194-1199 renders each swatch as a `<div class="swatch" @click=...>` with no role, no tabindex and no keydown handler. The file contains no keydown or tabindex anywhere. Its only keyboard-reachable controls are the search input (`@input` only, so Enter selects nothing), the filter and spectrum chips, the Random, Clear and Close buttons, the custom-hex Apply button, and each swatch's nested star `<button>`. That star is `opacity:0` and becomes visible only under `.swatch:hover` (CSS lines 492 and 505-508). It has no :focus or :focus-within rule, and the exceptions are already-favourited dyes and the Favourites section. The Custom colour header (1125) and the Favourites header (1238) are click-only divs.

I also looked for a keyboard fallback and found none in v4. harmony, comparison, gradient, mixer and accessibility each build a keyboard-capable DyeSelector/DyeGrid (dye-grid.ts:265 has a keydown handler) inside renderLeftPanel(). However, v4-layout.ts:601-602 passes the same mainPanel as both leftPanel and rightPanel, and renderRightPanel() calls clearContainer(right) first (harmony-tool.ts:1050, comparison-tool.ts:844). The in-tool selector is therefore wiped straight away. The drawer is the only picker left, and it feeds tools through v4-layout.ts:197-215.

A keyboard-only user can star a dye or pick a random one, but cannot choose a specific dye. Only the Random button and the custom-hex Apply produce a pick from the keyboard. This is a complete block for one group of users on a core path, so it is more than cosmetic. MEDIUM matches the brief's scale and the earlier grading.

That remediation plan scheduled it (REMEDIATION_PLAN.md:300), but it was never fixed. The last commits to the file do not touch swatch semantics, and nothing in git log references the web-app BUG-066. The finding should be filed as a carried-over open finding, not a new discovery. skeptic.evidence:
Reproduction worked out from the code:
1. Open /presets. `loadPresets()` runs `getPresets({search: undefined, sort, limit: PRESET_PAGE_LIMIT})`, which reaches `communityService.getPresets({status:'approved', sort, limit})`. That caches the key `presets:status=approved&sort=…&limit=…` (community-preset-service.ts:293).
2. Delete your own approved preset. preset-tool.ts:984 awaits `presetSubmissionService.deletePreset`, shows the deleteSuccess toast, then runs `void this.loadPresets()` at :986. That builds the same filters and therefore the same key, and the cache hit at :265-267 returns the old list without fetching. The deleted card is still shown for up to 5 minutes.
3. Clicking that card goes through `hybridPresetService.getPreset` to the cached `preset:<id>` entry, which the delete never removed, so the stale detail view opens.

The edit callback at preset-tool.ts:953 behaves the same way.

- No cache handling anywhere in preset-submission-service.ts. A grep for cache/Cache/communityPreset returned no lines.
- `git log 8ecb878f..HEAD` on community-preset-service.ts, hybrid-preset-service.ts and preset-tool.ts is empty, so the origin is MAIN.

skeptic.reason: The recursion is real, but the condition that triggers it practically cannot happen. In collection-service.ts:189-198, initialize() sets `initialized` only after loadFavorites/loadCollections. A migration save (:452-468) always notifies listeners, the notify functions (:1051-1062) call getX, and getX calls initialize() again, which re-reads storage. If the write did not stick, the data still needs migrating and the loop never ends. In practice the trigger is close to impossible. StorageService.getItem returns null whenever isAvailable() (storage-service.ts:47-60) fails its own probe write, so the loop needs localStorage that passes that small test write but rejects the migration write. The defect is real but I'd grade it LOW, not MEDIUM. In apps/web-app/src/main.ts:126, `await import('@components/tutorial-spotlight')` sits inside the same try block as critical init. tutorial-spotlight is imported only there, and it ships as its own 8.99 kB chunk (bundle-web-app.txt:37). If that import rejects, the catch at :151 calls renderFatalError, and container.replaceChildren (shared/fatal-error.ts:71) replaces the v4 shell that was already mounted. No test covers this: there is no main.test and no test references the spotlight.

Three things push the severity down:
1. The trigger is a fetch failure inside one request window during boot. It comes after the v4-layout chunk and the initial tool chunk have both loaded; initializeV4Layout awaits loadToolContent at v4-layout.ts:465.
2. It happens milliseconds after mount, before the user can have built any state. So the visible result is "boot failed, Reload" with a working Reload button, which is the same as the by-design fatal path for a v4-layout chunk failure one request earlier.
3. In the deploy-flip case, the page is stale anyway, so a reload is the right fix.

The result is a recoverable startup failure on a very rare transient, which fits "latent" better than "wrong result on an edge path". The fix direction stands: give the spotlight import its own try/catch, as loadToolContent (v4-layout.ts:727-747) and changelog-modal.ts:126-132 (BUG-090) already do for their chunks.

skeptic.reason:
The duplication is real; I could not refute it. A bot `/preset submit` goes through presets-api `POST /api/v1/presets` (discord-worker `services/preset-api.ts:304`). presets-api then always fires `notifyDiscordBot` (`presets.ts:1077-1091`). Nothing on that path filters on `auth.authSource`: the only authSource check (`:371`) is the web re-key. discord-worker's webhook (`index.ts:402` pending, `:446` approved) also ignores `preset.source`. Meanwhile `processSubmitCommand` posts its own embed to the same channel ids (`preset.ts:570-577`), so every bot submission produces two moderation or submission-log posts.

I grade it LOW, not MEDIUM. The harm is duplicate moderator and audit-log posts, and the revision binding defends every wrong action. The bot's twin uses legacy ids because `reviewCustomId` gets no revision (`preset-notifications.ts:96-110`). moderation-worker's `preset-moderation.ts:12-13` says a legacy click "never acts" and refreshes the message instead. So a moderator clicking the legacy twin loses one click and gets a refreshed embed, but no preset state goes wrong, nothing is lost and nobody is approved by mistake. Two Approve buttons with the same id were already harmless before PR #225. The submission-log double post is cosmetic and goes to an admin channel only.
skeptic.evidence:
- **Bot-side posts:** `apps/discord-worker/src/handlers/commands/preset.ts:570-577` calls `notifySubmissionChannel` and `notifyModerationChannel` unconditionally. The `:1142-1150` helper passes no `contentRevision`, so `reviewCustomId` returns the legacy form `preset_<kind>_<id>` (`apps/discord-worker/src/handlers/commands/preset-notifications.ts:96-110`).
- **presets-api notify:** `apps/presets-api/src/handlers/presets.ts:1074-1091` builds `submissionPayload` with `source: auth.authSource` and calls `notifyDiscordBot` for every caller. `apps/presets-api/src/services/notification-service.ts:177-237` skips the call only when the `DISCORD_WORKER` binding or `INTERNAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is missing. Production binds `DISCORD_WORKER` (`apps/presets-api/wrangler.toml:86-87`), and the secret is listed at `:99`.
- **Webhook posts:** `apps/discord-worker/src/index.ts:402` (pending) calls `sendModerationNotification` with `contentRevision`, and `:446-456` (approved) posts to `SUBMISSION_LOG_CHANNEL_ID`. Neither branch checks the source. Both paths use the same channel secrets (`apps/discord-worker/CLAUDE.md:55-57`) and the same token logic (`moderationToken`, `preset-notifications.ts:71-76`).
- **Why the twin is harmless:** `apps/moderation-worker/src/handlers/buttons/preset-moderation.ts:12-13,121` refreshes the message on a legacy click and never acts on the preset. That is why I put this at LOW (noise only) rather than MEDIUM.
- **Tests:** `preset.test.ts:1469` asserts the bot-side moderation post, so the duplication is locked in by a test rather than caught by one.
- **Repro:** I wrote no temporary test file. Every guard on the path is a plain conditional read above.

skeptic.reason: I could not refute this. When a web edit of an approved preset is flagged (or Perspective is unavailable), presets-api moves the preset to pending, stores the previous_values snapshot and fires the webhook. verdicts.reason: Four handlers await validateWorld before answering Discord: budget.ts:215 (find) and :504 (quick) before deferredResponse, plus budget.ts:450 (set_world) and preferences.ts:342, both fully synchronous with no defer. On a cold isolate validateWorld (universalis-client.ts:356-372) makes up to 2 sequential service-binding fetches with a 10 s timeout each (:79, :115). This is the same defect as BUG-008, which was rated MEDIUM. Exposure is narrowed by api-worker's per-colo Cache API (24 h TTL + 6 h SWR): it takes a full cache miss plus a slow Universalis.
verdicts.originEvidence: git show 8ecb878f:apps/discord-worker/src/handlers/commands/budget.ts has await resolveWorld at :215/:504, before deferredResponse() at :236/:520.
verdicts.repro: Cold discord-worker isolate plus an api-worker cache miss with slow Universalis: /budget find world:<DC name> exceeds 3 s and Discord shows 'The application did not respond'.
verdicts.fix: Defer first and run validateWorld inside ctx.waitUntil, for find/quick and also set_world and /preferences set (ephemeral defer). Or race the lookup against a ~2 s budget and degrade. No package publish.

skeptic.reason: I could not refute this, and I agree with MEDIUM. I re-derived it from the code. budget.ts:215 and :504 await resolveWorld before deferredResponse() at :236 and :520. budget.ts:450 and preferences.ts:342 await validateWorld and only then send a synchronous reply. Nothing at dispatch level races the handler or auto-defers it: the only Promise.race in discord-worker src is command-trace's drain deadline. BUG-008 (MEDIUM, fixed in 21ae7d5b) has the same mechanism: the same getCachedWorlds and getCachedDataCenters calls, behind the same api-worker cache. The api-worker 24 h + 6 h SWR cache narrows exposure equally in both cases, so it is no reason to downgrade.
skeptic.evidence:
- **Validation sits on the ack path.** apps/discord-worker/src/handlers/commands/budget.ts:144-152: resolveWorld always calls validateWorld when there is a world override or a stored prefs.world. Every /budget find and /budget quick that has a world pays for it before the ack, not only those with a typed override.
- **Timing on a cold cache.** apps/discord-worker/src/services/budget/universalis-client.ts:356-372: validateWorld runs getCachedWorlds, then (for a data-centre input) getCachedDataCenters, one after the other. Each has a 1 h module-scope cache (:86, :89-90) and REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 10000 (:79). Behind it, api-worker's /worlds and /data-centers (apps/api-worker/src/universalis/router.ts:343, :372) use cachedFetch with UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000 (apps/api-worker/src/universalis/services/cached-fetch.ts:51). Nothing on the path is shorter than Discord's 3 s.
- **The designed outage reply is never seen when Universalis is slow.** The BUG-031 'upstream' reply (budget.ts:222-228) arrives only after the 10 s abort, so the user gets "The application did not respond" instead.
- **No global guard.** Grepping apps/discord-worker/src (excluding tests) for Promise.race, autoDefer and withDeadline finds only services/command-trace.ts:233/262, which is the trace drain.
- **The precedent is the same mechanism.** apps/discord-worker/src/handlers/commands/manual.ts:386-396 documents the BUG-008 fix for exactly these getCachedWorlds/getCachedDataCenters calls, described as "10s timeout each on a cold cache".
- **Origin is MAIN.** At 8ecb878f, budget.ts has resolveWorld at :215 and :504, with deferredResponse() at :236 and :520, plus validateWorld at :450. preferences.ts has validateWorld at :342.
- **Not tested.** budget.test.ts:39 mocks validateWorld, so no test exercises a slow lookup before the ack.
- **Exposure is narrow.** It takes a cold or expired discord-worker isolate cache, a full api-worker per-colo Cache API miss and a slow Universalis all at once. That fits an edge path or operational risk (MEDIUM), not a common path.
- **No repro file.** I did not write the optional __repro__skeptic.test.ts, so there is nothing to delete.

(1) The JSON.parse arm is effectively unreachable: the blob's only writers in this repo use JSON.stringify (services/preferences.ts:285/345/166 and the dyeFilters writers at handlers/commands/preferences.ts:722/786), and a KV value is replaced atomically. (2) The only live trigger is a kv.get that rejects while a kv.put moments later in the same invocation succeeds, which is a partial KV fault. Since v5 deleted favorites and collections (CHANGELOG:683), no user content lives in this blob. BUG-036 already accepts silent loss of a write to this blob from a far likelier trigger (concurrent writes). The production [env.production.services] DISCORD_WORKER binding is present, and env-validation requires INTERNAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET. discord-worker's webhook posts any pending preset to MODERATION_CHANNEL_ID and any approved one to SUBMISSION_LOG_CHANNEL_ID. So every /preset submit produces two embeds: two submission-log lines when clean, or two moderation embeds when flagged. The bot-side moderation embed has no contentRevision, so it carries legacy ids that only refresh. The edit path is not always a duplicate. Bot-side notifyEditModerationChannel fires whenever the response's moderation_status is 'pending' (preset.ts:922-925). presets-api reports 'pending' for a tag-only or dye-only edit of an already-pending preset, where ownerEditOutcome gives notifiesModerators=false and sends no webhook. On that path the bot posts a lone moderation embed. That reopens the uncapped "PATCH tags pings moderators" path that FINDING-004 closed, limited only by the bot's per-user command rate limit. No wrong moderation action results: legacy clicks only refresh, and revision-bound clicks re-check status. The impact is moderator-channel duplication and noise plus an uncapped ping path, so MEDIUM as an operational risk is right; it is not HIGH.

skeptic.reason: I could not refute this. Both paths run on every bot submission, and both depend on the same discord-worker channel secrets, so neither can fire without the other. Path 1: presets-api calls notifyDiscordBot for every submit (presets.ts:1080-1091) and for every edit where notifiesModerators is true and the re-read row is pending (presets.ts:846-869). Neither branch checks authSource; it is only forwarded as `source`. notifyDiscordBot (notification-service.ts:177) gives up only when the DISCORD_WORKER binding or INTERNAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET is missing. The binding is in the production wrangler.toml and the secret is in the documented production set. The webhook (discord-worker index.ts:398-445) posts a pending preset to MODERATION_CHANNEL_ID and an approved one to SUBMISSION_LOG_CHANNEL_ID, whatever the `source`. Path 2: the bot's own handler then posts again on the same outcome. On submit, preset.ts:571 calls notifySubmissionChannel if the preset was approved and preset.ts:576 calls notifyModerationChannel if not. On edit, preset.ts:924 calls notifyEditModerationChannel when the result is pending. sendModerationNotification has no dedup. The bot's call passes no contentRevision, so its post carries legacy button ids. moderation-worker treats a legacy click as refresh-only (preset-moderation.ts:12-13,121), so every bot-submitted pending preset leaves a second queue entry whose buttons do nothing. One limit: an edit to an already-pending preset that changes no text (notifiesModerators=false) gets only the bot's post. Severity: MEDIUM, not HIGH. The impact is duplicate or dead-button entries in the moderator and log channels, an operational problem with no data loss and no wrong result for the author. It is not LOW either, because it happens on every bot submission and misleads moderators.

skeptic.reason: I couldn't refute it, and MEDIUM is the right severity. validatePresetDyes (validation-service.ts:227-256) checks the array length (3-6), that each id is an integer, and that it is a stainID in 1-254. It never checks that the ids are distinct. It is the only dye check on both submit (presets.ts:1413) and edit (presets.ts:1451). generateDyeSignature (preset-service.ts:40) sorts the ids but keeps repeats, so [7,7,7] passes validation and [1,2,3,3] gets a different UNIQUE dye_signature from [1,2,3]. A user can reach this through the bot: /preset submit (discord-worker preset.ts:424-462) collects dye1..dye6 and resolves each name with no dedupe. A preset whose content passes moderation is stored as 'approved' (presets.ts:994), so it goes into the public gallery with no review. The web-app form can't reach this path because it toggles a dye off when picked twice (preset-submission-form.ts:479-482). That makes this a one-client edge path that needs a deliberate or accidental repeat, so it is not HIGH. The rate limit of 10 submissions per day and later moderator hiding limit the damage but don't stop it. It is not LOW because what gets published is wrong: a "3-dye" palette made of one colour, or a near-duplicate that slips past the duplicate check. No test covers repeated ids.

skeptic.reason:
The defect is real. In apps/api-worker/src/index.ts, lines 128 and 129 both register the same telemetryRateLimitMiddleware instance, and Hono's `/v1/telemetry/*` pattern also matches the bare `/v1/telemetry`. The worker-kit factory (packages/worker-kit/src/middleware/rate-limit.ts) has no once-per-request guard, so every beacon calls the TELEMETRY_RATE_LIMITER binding twice under the same key. The origin is MAIN: both lines exist at 8ecb878f, added in 0bc669e4.

I grade it LOW, not MEDIUM. The only harm is lost analytics data points. Beacons go through sendBeacon, so the client ignores the response, and the TELEMETRY_LIMIT docblock says a dropped beacon "costs nothing but a data point". It only happens when one IP has more than about 30 opted-in tabs open, instead of the intended 60, and the native binding counts per colo. skeptic.evidence:
- **Reproduction:** I ran a temporary test, apps/api-worker/tests/__repro__skeptic.test.ts, against the real index.ts app and have deleted it; `git status` is clean. It bound TELEMETRY_RATE_LIMITER to a fake binding that allows 240 limit() calls.

- **Code:** apps/api-worker/src/index.ts:128-129 has `app.use(TELEMETRY_PATH, telemetryRateLimitMiddleware); app.use(`${TELEMETRY_PATH}/*`, telemetryRateLimitMiddleware);`.

- **Config:** wrangler.toml binds TELEMETRY_RATE_LIMITER at limit 240 / 60 s, namespace 1004 in dev and 1003 in production.
- **Origin:** `git show 8ecb878f:apps/api-worker/src/index.ts` already has both lines, so this is MAIN.
- **Tests:** no test drives a beacon through index.ts with the binding present and counts limit() calls. src/telemetry/router.test.ts uses the real app but does not assert the call count.
- **Why LOW:**

skeptic.reason:
The defect is real. It was already on MAIN at 8ecb878f and no test covers it. In C:/dev/XIVProjects/xivdyetools/.claude/worktrees/preview-2026-10-04/apps/oauth/src/index.ts:184 the limiter takes `new URL(c.req.url).pathname`, which stays percent-encoded. That raw path picks the tier in getOAuthLimit (packages/worker-kit/src/rate-limiter/presets/configs.ts:45-51, a startsWith match) and is also part of the bucket key `${ip}:${path}` in apps/oauth/src/services/rate-limit.ts. Hono 4.13.9 routes on the decoded path instead (node_modules/hono/dist/utils/url.js getPath calls tryDecodeURI), so every spelling of the same route reaches the same handler but counts against its own bucket.

Severity stays MEDIUM, not higher, for three reasons:
(1) The real problem is the bucket split, not the tier. A wrong tier can even be stricter: /auth/xivauth/%63allback matches the '/auth/xivauth' prefix and gets 10/min instead of 20.
(2) A per-IP limit can already be beaten by rotating IPs. The POST callback also needs a validly signed state with a matching PKCE challenge (FINDING-012) before Discord is called, so the bypass does not let anyone guess codes or skip auth. What it allows is unthrottled traffic from one IP, which is load on Discord's token endpoint and an operational risk.
(3) Whether the production zone decodes %63 before the Worker sees it ("Normalize URLs to origin") is not recorded in the repo. Cloudflare's own rate-limiting docs warn that different path spellings can reach the origin without matching a rule.

Neither point refutes the defect. Both argue against raising it above MEDIUM.
skeptic.evidence:
I wrote my own repro, apps/oauth/src/__tests__/__repro__skeptic.test.ts, ran it alone, and deleted it (git status for apps/oauth is clean). It used createProductionEnv with counting fakes for RL_AUTH_10/20/30 that keep a separate count per key and return success while the count is at or under the limit, which models the native binding. It sent 35 requests per path with CF-Connecting-IP fixed:
- POST /auth/callback: 400 "Missing code or code_verifier" from the POST handler, limit 20, first 429 at index 20, key rl:1.2.3.4:/auth/callback:t20_60.
- POST /auth/%63allback: the same 400 from the same POST handler, but limit 30, first 429 at index 30, and a separate key rl:1.2.3.4:/auth/%63allback:t30_60.
- GET /auth/%64iscord: routed to the Discord authorize handler (400 "Missing code_challenge"), limit 30 instead of 10, own key.
- POST /auth/xivauth/%63allback: reached the POST handler with limit 10 instead of 20, so here the wrong tier is stricter.

Each letter of the path can be encoded or not, and the hex digits can be upper or lower case, so one IP gets hundreds of independent buckets per route and the per-IP limit stops working. `git show 8ecb878f:apps/oauth/src/index.ts` has the same line at 184, so the origin is MAIN. No test in apps/oauth/src/__tests__ sends an encoded /auth path. The fix direction holds: key and tier on c.req.path, the decoded path Hono routes on.

skeptic.reason: I could not refute it, and MEDIUM is the right severity. In HSL mode, mixing an exactly grey colour gives a colour with a hue neither input has. rgbToHsl returns h:0 for any grey (packages/core/src/blending/conversions.ts:240-242), and blendHSL at packages/core/src/blending/blending.ts:187 blends that 0 as if it were a real hue. Nothing on the path special-cases grey: the web mixer, ColorService.mixColorsHsl, and bot-logic gradient.ts:210 (hsl calls blendColors) all reach blendHSL unchanged. The 'hsl' choice is offered in apps/discord-worker/src/commands/schemas.ts:415 (/gradient), :465 (/mixer) and :646 (the /mixer default setting). Three real dyes are exactly grey (Slate Grey #656565, Jet Black #1e1e1e, Metallic Silver #a7a7a7), and the bot and web tools also accept raw hex such as #FFFFFF. It is not HIGH because HSL is not the default mode and the input must be exactly grey; that is a wrong result on an edge path, which the brief calls MEDIUM. It is not LOW because nothing else blocks it and the result is visibly wrong.
skeptic.evidence:
I re-ran it with a temporary packages/core/src/blending/__repro__skeptic.test.ts, then deleted it. blendColors(...,'hsl',0.5) returned:
- #FFFFFF + #0000FF gave #df9fdf (pink, not light blue).
- #000000 + #00FF00 gave #606020 (olive).
- Jet Black #1e1e1e + #0000FF gave #762776 (magenta).
- Metallic Silver #a7a7a7 + #2c7fb8 (hue about 205) gave #9b69b0 (purple).

Code path: rgbToHsl sends max===min to {h:0, s:0} (conversions.ts:240-242). blendHSL passes hsl1.h straight to interpolateHue (blending.ts:187). For white + blue, the 'shorter' rule turns diff 240 into -120, so the hue lands on 300 (magenta) at t=0.5.

No test covers this:
- ColorService.test.ts:432 only checks s===0 for grey.
- conversions.equivalence.test.ts:276 pins the current #644216+#000000 hsl output, so it will need updating with the fix.

skeptic.reason: The defect is real. At HarmonySelector.ts:224 `used` starts empty, and a pin only enters `used` when the loop reaches its own slot. So an earlier slot left unpinned can still choose the pinned dye, even with preventDuplicates on. It is not reachable from a single UI action: harmony-tool only pins a dye picked from that slot's own companions (onSwapDye at :1524, handleSwapDye at :1688), and under preventDuplicates those companions already leave out every dye an earlier slot holds. My sweep of all 2,750 single-pin cases found 0 duplicates when the config stays the same. It only shows up when a config change leaves the pin in place (:360-393 clears swappedDyes only when the wheel changes) and moves an earlier slot's pick onto the pinned dye. That happened in 3 of 2,750 cases after switching strict matching on, 1 of 2,750 with strict on plus cie76, and 0 when the companion count changed. The pin lives only in memory, and changing the base, the harmony type or the wheel clears it. The result is a visible repeated dye that the user can fix by swapping again, with no data loss. That is an extremely rare, cosmetic edge, so it is LOW, not MEDIUM.

In triadic, slot 1 is the last slot, and Jet Black is never slot 0's pick, so the uniqueness assertion at HarmonySelector.test.ts:213 can never fail. The comment there says "a later slot cannot reuse it", but no later slot exists. No other test reserves a pin against earlier slots: the golden tests don't, and the web-app harmony-tool.test.ts only checks that pins clear when the wheel changes. The underlying defect (core-color-02) is also real. In HarmonySelector.ts, `used` gets a pin's id only when the loop reaches that pin's slot, so earlier slots can still pick that dye. However, the single-render path that core-color-02 describes cannot happen in the UI. Swaps come only from a slot's companion list (harmony-tool.ts:1524/1629). Under preventDuplicates those companions already leave out the dyes earlier slots chose, and pins at later slots never change earlier slots. A search found no duplicate from that path. The duplicate needs an extra step: a swap, then a config change the web app keeps pins across (dedup toggle, ΔE method, perceptual toggle, filters; only a wheel, type or base change clears them, harmony-tool.ts:385-396). Even then the harm is one dye shown twice in the palette. A test gap for an edge path that needs a swap plus a setting change, with only display harm, is LOW, not MEDIUM.

verdicts.title: PaletteService kMeansClustering caps k at pixel count, so images with fewer distinct colours than colorCount return duplicate 0-pixel clusters that discord /extractor renders as rows
verdicts.reason: Once every distinct colour is a centroid, k-means++ :166-168 picks a duplicate pixel. Strict < in assignToClusters gives the clone 0 pixels and updateCentroids keeps it. discord extractor.ts:525-556 has no pixelCount filter: dedupe swaps each clone to a 'next best' dye, bandSlices gives it 7px, and the count inflates. web-app filters it and documents this exact case at extractor-tool.ts:2145-2158.
verdicts.repro: A PNG at or under maxDimension (no Lanczos resize, so no edge colours) with 2 opaque colours, run with colorCount 4: the result is [red 50, blue 50, red 0, red/blue 0], and the card shows two fabricated 0% rows
verdicts.evidence:
PaletteService.ts:166-168, :272 effectiveK=min(k,pixels.length), :186-205 strict < assignment; extractor.ts:525-556 has no filter
web-app extractor-tool.ts:2145-2158 comment plus .filter(pixelCount>0)
verdicts.originEvidence: git show 8ecb878f:packages/core/src/services/PaletteService.ts has effectiveK at :272. git log 8ecb878f..HEAD -- packages/core apps/discord-worker/src/handlers/commands/extractor.ts is empty.
verdicts.fix:
Drop pixelCount===0 clusters in core extractPalette (or cap k at the distinct-colour count) and assert the exact result. Needs a @xivdyetools/core publish, then consumer deploys.
App-only alternative: filter pixelCount>0 in discord-worker extractor.ts before dedupe; no publish needed.

skeptic.reason: I could not refute this. I traced the code path and reproduced it. At PaletteService.ts:272, effectiveK = min(k, pixels.length) caps k by pixel count, not by distinct colours. Once every distinct colour is already a centroid, the total squared distance is 0 and :166-168 picks a random pixel, which is a duplicate centroid. assignToClusters (:213-218) uses strict <, so ties go to the lower index and the clone gets 0 pixels. updateCentroids (:242-244) keeps the empty clone, and extractPalette (:420-427) returns it with dominance 0 and pixelCount 0. Nothing downstream filters it out. extractAndMatchPalette (:459-485) still matches a dye for it. In discord extractor.ts:525-559, dedupe (:111-156) swaps the duplicate dye for the next-best dye, and the result is added to both band and rows. The svg bandSlices MIN_SLICE=7 (palette-grid.ts:105-118) then gives it a visible slice. The embed count at :589 also says "4 colours", so the I18N-006 comment there, which says matches.length===1 is reachable for a near-monochrome image, is wrong. The input is reachable from Discord: MIN_COLORS is 3 and the default is 4 (extractor.ts:68-74), so any lossless image with fewer distinct colours than that triggers it. That covers flat icons or pixel art up to 256px (no resize), and solid-colour images at any size, since a Lanczos resize of a single colour stays a single colour. No test covers it: the core tests always set colorCount equal to the number of distinct colours, the clamp test (PaletteService.test.ts ~131-140) only asserts length ≤10 / ≥1, and the discord tests mock extractAndMatchPalette. Origin is MAIN. I am keeping MEDIUM rather than LOW because the card shows made-up dye recommendations and a wrong colour count, not just cosmetic noise. I am not raising it to HIGH because it needs a flat-colour lossless image; photos and JPEGs produce many distinct colours.
skeptic.evidence: I wrote a temporary repro at packages/core/src/services/__tests__/__repro__skeptic.test.ts, ran it on its own, and then deleted it (git status shows it is gone). It fed 50 red + 50 blue pixels to extractPalette with colorCount 4 and ran 20 times. Every run returned 4 entries, exactly 2 of them with pixelCount 0, and the test passed. The web-app works around this same case: extractor-tool.ts:2150-2158 has a comment ("a flat logo asked for four colours returns two real clusters and two empty ones") and applies .filter(cluster => cluster.pixelCount > 0). discord-worker has no such filter at extractor.ts:525-559. Origin check: git show 8ecb878f:packages/core/src/services/PaletteService.ts has effectiveK at :272, and git log 8ecb878f..HEAD on PaletteService.ts and extractor.ts is empty. One note: packages/core/src/services/dye/__tests__/__repro__skeptic.test.ts was already untracked before I started; it belongs to another session and I left it alone.

skeptic.reason: The defect is real and happens as described, but it is a cosmetic truncated label, not a wrong result. The steps option allows up to 12 (apps/discord-worker/src/commands/schemas.ts:399-400). capGradientRows (packages/bot-logic/src/commands/gradient.ts:106-116) merges adjacent steps that land on the same dye, and :310 turns a merged range into the text `${start}–${end}`. That text is the row lead (packages/svg/src/gradient.ts:173), which gets 28 px (:103). frame.ts:570 draws it with fitText(lead, 28, 13, 'mono'), and at 13 px mono each character is counted as 8.06 px (frame.ts:181, base.ts estimateTextWidth; the en dash is not counted as wide). So '9–10' measures 32.2 px and becomes '9–…', and '10–12' measures 40.3 px and becomes '10…'. A single '10' to '12' measures 24.2 px and fits. No test uses a range with two digits. I put it at LOW rather than MEDIUM because nothing shown is wrong: the dye name, the ΔE and the swatch pair on the row are still correct, and the strip at the top still shows every step. The ellipsis shows the label was cut rather than giving a false value. It also needs 10 or more steps plus a merge in the tail of the gradient. Under the brief's scale that is cosmetic, so LOW.
skeptic.evidence: packages/svg/src/gradient.ts:103 `const ROW_WIDTHS: MeasuredRowWidths = { lead: 28, pair: 56, name: 178, bar: 34, measure: 32 };` (its doc comment at :95 says lead 28 holds a "2–3" range, which only covers single digits); packages/svg/src/frame.ts:570 `fitText(o.lead, w.lead, CARD_TYPE.value, 'mono')` with CARD_TYPE.value=13 (frame.ts:34) and the 0.62 mono factor (frame.ts:181); fitText's pop loop (frame.ts:197-201) gives '9–…' and '10…'; packages/bot-logic/src/commands/gradient.ts:310 builds stepText; apps/discord-worker/src/commands/schemas.ts:400 max_value: 12. I ran no repro test because the width arithmetic is deterministic and was checked by hand against the code.

For '123456' or '333333', n is at least 5729, so it calls getDyeById, which returns null because the highest legacyItemID in dyes.json is 48227. The function then returns null at :212 and never reaches the hex check. Its own docstring (:190) says it accepts 'FF0000' without '#', and isValidHex says the '#' is optional. Before 2026-08-29 these inputs resolved to the hex colour, so this is a regression from that change. The CHANGELOG entry for it names only the 3-digit shorthand as an accepted ambiguity. A hex with a leading zero that happens to equal a legacy item id has a quieter failure: '013114' resolves to the dye Pure White instead of the colour #013114, with no error. Nothing upstream catches it. The discord-worker handlers (gradient.ts:55/68, mixer-v4.ts:51/59, harmony.ts:60, contrast.ts:56, accessibility.ts:64, comparison.ts:21, extractor.ts:90) pass the raw option value straight in and reply errors.invalidColor. Stoat-worker partly recovers: its fallback to resolveDyeInput (:306) returns the closest dye instead of the exact hex. No test covers it. input-resolution.test.ts tests only '#123456' (:162) and alphanumeric 'FF0000' (:150), and nothing grep finds anywhere tests an all-digit 6-char hex without '#'. Two points argue against going higher. The option hints in schemas.ts:161/302/382/389 show the '#' form, and the usual failure is a visible invalidColor error that a retry with '#' fixes. Still, it is a wrong result for valid input on an edge path. It is not cosmetic, latent, or defended elsewhere, so MEDIUM is correct and HIGH is not warranted.
skeptic.evidence: packages/bot-logic/src/input-resolution.ts:40-45 (`/^\s*(\d{1,6})\s*$/`; n in 1-254 calls getByStainId, n >= 5729 calls getDyeById, anything else returns null), :49-51 isBareNumber, :208-214 (bare number checked before hex; returns null when parseDyeIdInput misses), :217 isValidHex not reached, :190 docstring promises 'FF0000'. packages/core/src/data/dyes.json legacyItemID min 5729, max 48227. packages/bot-logic/CHANGELOG.md 2026-08-29 'Added' entry names only the 3-digit shorthand ambiguity. apps/discord-worker/src/handlers/commands/gradient.ts:55-77 passes raw input and replies errors.invalidColor. apps/stoat-worker/src/services/dye-resolver.ts:54 falls back to resolveDyeInput, which returns the closest dye. packages/bot-logic/src/input-resolution.test.ts:144-167 and :387-431 contain no all-digit 6-char hex case. apps/discord-worker/src/commands/schemas.ts:161/382/389 hints use '#FF5733' / '#FF0000'. verdicts.title: ci.yml workflow-level concurrency ci-${{ github.ref }} + cancel-in-progress: true cancels main-push and nightly-schedule runs against each other
verdicts.reason: ci.yml:42-44 is a workflow-level group keyed only on ref with cancel-in-progress: true; main pushes and the schedule both resolve to refs/heads/main. A batch merge cancels every run but the last (whose ...[HEAD^] filter only diffs that commit), and an 11:17 schedule run (audit-only, ci/e2e skipped by `if != schedule`) cancels an in-flight push run.
verdicts.repro: Merge 2+ PRs to main within minutes (or push just before 11:17 UTC) -> earlier main runs show cancelled; their changed packages never get a post-merge CI run
verdicts.evidence: ci.yml:42-44 (concurrency), :98/:134/:339 (`if: github.event_name != 'schedule'`); no workflow_run gating anywhere; git show 8ecb878f:.github/workflows/ci.yml lines 42-44 identical
verdicts.originEvidence: git show 8ecb878f:.github/workflows/ci.yml -> lines 42-44 same group/cancel-in-progress: true
verdicts.fix: cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}, or add github.event_name (and sha for push) to the group. No package publish.

skeptic.reason:
The mechanism is real, but it costs only a redundant post-merge signal, so I'd grade it LOW, not MEDIUM. In .github/workflows/ci.yml:42-44 the concurrency group is `ci-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: true`. Main pushes and the 11:17 schedule both resolve to refs/heads/main, so a batch merge leaves only the last push run alive, and that run's `...[HEAD^]` filters cover only its own commit. A schedule run can also cancel a push run that is still going. No production result is wrong, though:
- Each PR was already gated by its own pull_request CI (refs/pull/N/merge), and that CI is the real gate.
- No deploy workflow waits on CI. They have their own groups and no workflow_run or needs link to ci.yml, so a cancelled main run blocks and alters nothing.
- Batch merges are already covered by the local preview/integration branch, which runs the gates over the combined tree.
- When a push cancels the nightly run, nothing is lost, because `audit` has no `if` and runs on push too.
- The schedule overlap needs a push run still going at 11:17 UTC (about 07:17 maintainer time), which is rare.
So this is LOW: latent and covered by PR CI. The suggested fix is also incomplete: with `cancel-in-progress: false`, GitHub still keeps only one pending run per group, so merging 3 or more PRs still drops the middle runs. The group key needs `github.event_name` plus `github.sha` (or `run_id`) for push and schedule events.
skeptic.evidence: ci.yml:42-44: `concurrency: group: ci-${{ github.ref }} / cancel-in-progress: true`. This has not changed since 9af84394 (2026-02-18), so it is MAIN. ci.yml:98, :134 and :339: `if: github.event_name != 'schedule'` on secret-scan, ci and e2e; the audit job (:59) has no `if`, so it runs on every push. ci.yml:9: `push: branches: [main, master, '*-prep']`; ci.yml:33: `cron: '17 11 * * *'`. The deploy-*.yml workflows have independent concurrency groups (for example deploy-api-worker, cancel-in-progress: false), and grep finds no `workflow_run` and no cross-workflow `needs` in .github/workflows. The only `needs:` is publish-packages.yml:95, which is internal to that file. On a PR event HEAD^ is the base tip (comment at ci.yml:13-15), so each PR's affected packages were tested against the combined tree before merge. GitHub concurrency semantics keep at most one pending run per group, so `cancel-in-progress: false` alone does not save intermediate push runs. No test covers workflow concurrency.

verdicts.title: publish-packages.yml Publish loop records FAILED+= and keeps publishing dependents of a failed package
verdicts.reason: Loop (155-163) never skips later packages after a failure; svg/bot-logic use workspace:* on core, which pnpm rewrites to core's unpublished local version. release-process.md:56-58 itself says such a consumer fails to install for external users. Self-heals only after core is republished.

verdicts.originEvidence: git show 8ecb878f:.github/workflows/publish-packages.yml -> FAILED+=("$pkg") at :161, no break/skip
verdicts.fix: Do not blanket-break (TIER_ORDER puts worker-kit before svg); skip any later package whose workspace: deps include a FAILED one, and in single-package mode verify each workspace dep version exists on npm. Workflow-only, no package publish.

skeptic.reason:
The defect is real. The Publish loop at /c/dev/XIVProjects/xivdyetools/.claude/worktrees/preview-2026-10-04/.github/workflows/publish-packages.yml:155-164 appends a failed package to FAILED (line 161) and carries on to the next package. It never checks whether that next package depends on the one that failed. svg and bot-logic depend on core through `workspace:*`, so a run where core fails can still publish svg and bot-logic pinned to a core version that is not on npm. The loop is byte-identical at main@8ecb878f, so the origin is MAIN, and no test covers the workflow.

I grade it LOW rather than MEDIUM, for five reasons:
1. It only happens at publish time, after Build and Test have already passed for every selected package. The dependency's own `pnpm publish` has to fail mid-run, and it has to be a failure specific to that package, such as one package's trusted-publisher config. A transient network or OIDC fault would usually fail the dependents too.
2. The failure is loud. The job exits 1 with a "Failed to publish core" annotation, so it is never a silent bad release.
3. It fixes itself. Rerunning `all-modified` publishes core, which is still behind npm, and skips svg and bot-logic, which are already at the new version. The pinned core version then exists and the broken range resolves.
4. No first-party app is affected, because every app consumes these packages through `workspace:*`.
5. During the window, an external `npm install` of the new svg or bot-logic fails outright with ETARGET. Nobody gets a silently wrong result.

On the brief's scale that makes it latent and defended elsewhere, so LOW. It is not an edge-path wrong result.
skeptic.evidence:
- **The loop never skips dependents:** /c/dev/XIVProjects/xivdyetools/.claude/worktrees/preview-2026-10-04/.github/workflows/publish-packages.yml:155-170. Line 161 runs `FAILED+=("$pkg")` with no break and no check of the next package's deps. Line 169 runs `exit 1` only after the loop finishes.
- **Order:** TIER_ORDER at lines 56-64 is types, logger, auth, core, worker-kit, svg, bot-logic.
- **Build and Test run before Publish:** lines 125-143.
- **`workspace:*` deps:** /c/dev/XIVProjects/xivdyetools/.claude/worktrees/preview-2026-10-04/packages/svg/package.json:33 and /c/dev/XIVProjects/xivdyetools/.claude/worktrees/preview-2026-10-04/packages/bot-logic/package.json:37-38.
- **Origin MAIN:** `git show 8ecb878f:.github/workflows/publish-packages.yml` shows the same loop.
- **The docs state the hazard:** /c/dev/XIVProjects/xivdyetools/.claude/worktrees/preview-2026-10-04/docs/developer-guides/release-process.md:57-59.
- **Self-heal:** the detect job at lines 67-78 republishes only packages whose local version differs from npm, so a rerun publishes core alone.

skeptic.reason: I could not refute it, and MEDIUM is the right severity. A /preset submit that lands as pending sends two moderation posts to MODERATION_CHANNEL_ID, and a pending /preset edit does too. Nothing on the path filters by source or deduplicates. The duplicate cannot cause a wrong moderation decision, because legacy ids only refresh and bound ids carry a revision, so this is not HIGH. It is more than cosmetic, though. For bot edits, the only embed that shows the diff and the Revert button is the legacy copy, whose first click acts on nothing. The bound copy from the webhook is a plain "new pending" embed with no Revert, and it goes stale once the first decision is made. That is an operational risk on an edge path. Clean bot submissions also post twice to SUBMISSION_LOG_CHANNEL_ID; on its own that part would be LOW.

skeptic.evidence:
Defect it hides (gap1-01), traced from the code:
- gradient-tool.ts:175 sets the field to `{ ...DEFAULT_DYE_FILTERS }`.
- The constructor (:245-251) reads displayOptions, matchingMethod and preventDuplicates from getConfig('gradient'), but not dyeFilters.
- swatch-tool.ts:246 sets the same default. Swatch never calls getConfig('swatch'); its only getConfig call is for 'market' (:392).
- config-controller.ts:346-361: subscribe() only registers a listener and never fires it on registration.
- The only way into a tool's dyeFilters is the sidebar's handleDyeFiltersChange (config-sidebar.ts:885-907), which runs only on a user toggle. v4-layout.ts:192 forwards the key as `dyeFilters.<name>`, so it never reaches the tool's `config.dyeFilters` branch.

The only gradient/swatch hits are swatch-tool.test.ts:727 and :731, both inside not.toThrow. Other hits are in dye-filters-v4, config-sidebar, dye-filter-utils and dye-service tests, and none of them constructs either tool.
- No open PR touches these four files (git log 8ecb878f..HEAD is empty), so the origin is MAIN.

Walking the code path myself shows a flagged web edit of an approved preset becomes 'pending' and reaches the moderation channel only through presets-api's webhook. The webhook handler at apps/discord-worker/src/index.ts:407 always passes kind:'new'. Perspective being unavailable also counts as flagged (presets.ts:704-722), so while it is down every web edit of an approved preset takes this path. That makes MEDIUM the right grade, not LOW.

skeptic.reason:
I could not refute it. apps/og-worker/src/services/svg/gradient.ts:38-44 picks the ramp's colour space from `algo`: Oklab for oklab, RGB for rgb/distinguish/redmean, and Lab (mixColorsLab, :43) for everything else, including the default ciede2000. The page ramps in `this.colorSpace` instead (apps/web-app/src/components/gradient-tool.ts:1718-1771 and :1834). That defaults to 'hsv' (:96) and is sent in the share link as `interpolation` (:1691). The worker never reads that parameter: og-data-generator.ts:825-829 parses only start, end, steps and algo, the image URL (:315) does not carry it, and `interpolation` is not in OG_ALLOWED_QUERY_KEYS (index.ts:216). gradient.test.ts does not check which space the middle dyes are ramped in. The defect is already on main.

One point argues against raising the severity, and it also limits the proposed fix. The page's default stepCount is 8 (gradient-tool.ts:95), but the card is capped at BAND_CAP = 5 (band.ts:54, applied at gradient.ts:66). So in the default case the card samples different points along the ramp than the page does, and its middle dyes could never match the page one for one. A fix to the interpolation space alone gives exact parity only for shares with steps ≤ 5.

Against lowering it: on the default path (hsv, ciede2000, 8 steps) the mismatch still changes which dyes the card shows. For Jet Black→Canary Yellow the card shows greens (Mud, Moss, Lime), the page's 8-step HSV ramp shows mostly browns, and a card ramped in HSV would also show browns. The repo has treated this kind of card-vs-page drift as a bug before: mixer `mode` was added 2026-09-03, and commit 35914823 made the harmony card draw the harmony the page draws. The page itself is correct, so this is wrong output on a secondary surface (the link preview), not data loss. MEDIUM stands.

skeptic.reason: I could not refute this. Nothing on the path filters by source. A /preset submit through the bot authenticates to presets-api with authSource 'bot' (presets-api auth.ts:284/344). presets-api then calls notifyDiscordBot for every authSource, both on submit (presets.ts:1076-1093) and on a pending edit (presets.ts:845-871). notifyDiscordBot only checks that DISCORD_WORKER and INTERNAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET exist (notification-service.ts:183). Both are bound or required in production. discord-worker's webhook handler (index.ts:402 pending, :445 approved) also never checks preset.source; it reads source only to label the embed. When presets-api replies, the bot posts again itself: preset.ts:570-577 on submit, notifySubmissionChannel if approved or notifyModerationChannel if pending, and preset.ts:922-925 (notifyEditModerationChannel) on a pending edit. The result is two moderation embeds for every pending bot submission or edit, and two submission-log posts for every clean, auto-approved bot submission. The approved case is the common path, not an edge. The same code exists at 8ecb878f (presets.ts:1037/825, preset.ts:571/576/924, index.ts:402/445), so the origin is MAIN. MEDIUM is the right severity, not HIGH. Only the moderator and log channels see the duplicates. No user-visible result is wrong and no data is lost. The second copy also fails safely: per preview-image.ts:176 a legacy-id click only refreshes the embed (I checked the preview-image handler; I assumed the preset review buttons act the same, and on a duplicate a stale revision or status check stops the second action). So the cost is operational noise and confusion in the moderation queue, which is borderline LOW but fits "operational risk".

skeptic.reason: The defect is real: on a non-404 failure the preset's UUID is saved as its name and never looked up again. I would grade it LOW, not MEDIUM. Only the label in the `/preset favorite remove` autocomplete is wrong. The choice value is still the correct id, so removing the favourite still works. `/preset favorite list` reads only the ids and is not affected. Removing the favourite and adding it again stores the real name, so the user can recover. The trigger is narrow: a user with v1 favourites, which have had no names since the 2026-07-18 migration, who has not opened this autocomplete since then, and whose first use lands during a presets-api failure. Rate limiting is not a trigger, because service-binding calls skip the public per-IP limit.
skeptic.evidence:
Checked in the worktree at C:/dev/XIVProjects/xivdyetools/.claude/worktrees/preview-2026-10-04.

- apps/discord-worker/src/services/preset-api.ts:237-245: `getPreset` returns null only on a 404. Every other error is rethrown, and `request()` (:161-180) turns a non-ok response, a fetch error or the 10 s `AbortSignal.timeout` into a `PresetAPIError`.
- apps/discord-worker/src/index.ts:1291: `entries.filter((e) => !e.name)` selects only entries with an empty name.
- index.ts:1293: `presetApi.getPreset(env, e.id).catch(() => null)` turns any of those errors into null.
- index.ts:1296: `missing[i].name = resolved[i]?.name ?? missing[i].id` then stores the id as the name.
- index.ts:1307: `savePresetFavoriteEntries` writes the result to the v2 key.
- preset-favorites.ts:85 keeps any non-empty string name, so the next keystroke's `!e.name` filter never selects that entry again. The UUID label is permanent, and typing the preset's name no longer matches it (the query filter at :1316 compares against the name).

Why I grade it lower:
- The choice value at :1319 is still `e.id`, so removal works.
- preset.ts:1371 `/preset favorite list` reads only the ids through `getPresetFavorites`, so the list is not affected.
- The only add path, preset.ts:1238, saves `preset.name`, so removing and re-adding the favourite fixes the label.
- presets-api rate-limit.ts skips the per-IP limiter when `CF-Connecting-IP` is absent, as it is on service-binding calls. `getPreset` sends no user id, so no per-user limit applies either. A 429 burst is not a realistic trigger; it takes a 5xx, a D1 error or a timeout.
