verdicts.title: oauth /auth/* rate limiter keys and tiers on the raw percent-encoded pathname while Hono routes on the decoded path
verdicts.originEvidence: git show 8ecb878f:apps/oauth/src/index.ts:184 `const path = new URL(c.req.url).pathname;`; rate-limit.ts checkRateLimit key `${ip}:${path}` with getOAuthLimit(path).
verdicts.repro: POST /auth/%63allback repeatedly -> routed to the callback handler (400 'Missing code') on all 25 requests at the 30/min default tier with its own bucket, while literal /auth/callback 429s at request 21
verdicts.evidence: Temp repro (deleted) via app.fetch with the memory limiter: literal path 429 at request 21; the encoded path returned 400 for all 25. hono 4.13.9 utils/url.js:68-79 getPath decodeURI's the path.
verdicts.fix: Derive the limiter path from c.req.path (decoded, what Hono matched) for both getOAuthLimit and the key; add a test posting an encoded spelling past the limit. oauth-only, no publish.
verdicts.reason: Real in the Worker: each encoded spelling gets its own 30/min bucket and skips the 10/20 tiers. Whether production request.url arrives un-decoded on the auth.xivdyetools.app custom domain depends on zone URL-normalization settings the repo cannot show; kept at MEDIUM as an operational risk.

skeptic.reason: The defect is real and I reproduced it, but MEDIUM is too high. In apps/oauth/src/index.ts:184 the limiter key and tier come from the raw `new URL(c.req.url).pathname`. Hono 4.13.9 routes on the decoded path: getPath in node_modules/hono/dist/utils/url.js calls tryDecodeURI as soon as it sees a '%'. getOAuthLimit in packages/worker-kit/src/rate-limiter/presets/configs.ts:45 does a startsWith match on the raw path, so every encoded spelling falls through to the 30/min default tier and gets its own bucket. No existing test covers this. I'd grade it LOW for three reasons. (1) Only a single-IP attacker gains anything. The limit is already per-IP and per-colo, so anyone rotating IPs is unaffected, and none of the guarded endpoints protects a secret that could be brute-forced (PKCE-bound Discord/XIVAuth codes, signed JWTs). The worst outcome is extra upstream token-exchange calls, which IP rotation already allows. (2) Whether production is exposed depends on the auth.xivdyetools.app zone's URL-normalization settings. Those are not in the repo, and normalization that decodes unreserved percent-escapes before the Worker would close the gap. So this is latent defense-in-depth, not a demonstrated live bypass. (3) The bodySizeLimit and jsonDepthLimit middlewares and the handlers' own validation still run on every encoded request. The fix is still worth doing: key and tier on c.req.path.
skeptic.evidence: I ran a temporary test, apps/oauth/src/__tests__/__repro__skeptic.test.ts (now deleted; git status is clean). It sent 14 GETs from one CF-Connecting-IP through the real app with fetchWithEnv. Results: `/auth/discord limit=10` gave 302 x10, then 429 x4. `/auth/%64iscord limit=30` gave 302 x14. `/%61uth/discord limit=30` gave 302 x14. Encoded spellings therefore route to the handler, skip the 10/min login tier, and each gets its own bucket. Relevant code: apps/oauth/src/index.ts:183-190 (`app.use('/auth/*')`, `const path = new URL(c.req.url).pathname`, checkRateLimit), apps/oauth/src/services/rate-limit.ts checkRateLimit (`getOAuthLimit(path)` with the key `${ip}:${path}`), and hono getPath, which decodes whenever charCode 37 is present. The production exposure question (zone URL normalization on the custom domain) cannot be answered from the repo.

verdicts.title: reconcileTombstones tombstones saved presets after a swallowed API failure, for saved local- palettes, and against a stale filtered response
verdicts.originEvidence: 8ecb878f: preset-tool.ts:598 offline from isAPIAvailable(), :631 guard on the current searchQuery; hybrid-preset-service.ts:316 swallows the API-leg failure.
verdicts.repro: Transient 5xx on GET /presets (no cache hit) -> hybrid returns local-only, apiCount 0 < 50, offline=false -> every saved community preset marked 'Removed by its author' and hidden from Saved (keepDeleted off) until the next good load
verdicts.evidence: community-preset-service.ts:276-286 throws on non-ok; hybrid :315-317 catches and only warns; apiAvailable is set once at init (:128). preset-card.ts:428 shows Save on local- cards (isFromAPI false, so never 'live'). A stale filtered response lands after searchQuery is cleared.
verdicts.fix: getPresets reports apiOk; loadPresets uses a seq plus the captured query and drops stale responses; reconcile requires apiOk and an empty fetched query, and skips local- ids. Also count API rows before hybrid's sort+slice: 15 curated + up to 50 API rows are sliced to 50, so stable/name sorts can drop API rows and get under the BUG-020 full-page guard.
verdicts.reason: All three triggers verified; recovery happens on the next successful load. Not SUPERSEDED: the DEAD row on hybrid getPresets covers only the unreachable 'community' branch, and :315 is the live merge path. The slice issue is noted but not demonstrated, so it does not raise severity.

skeptic.reason: Not refuted; all three triggers hold in the code. (1) Swallowed failure: community-preset-service.ts:276-301 throws on non-ok responses and on timeouts. hybrid-preset-service.ts:315-317 catches the error and only warns, then returns the curated list. apiAvailable is set once at :128 and never cleared, so preset-tool.ts:598 keeps offline=false. apiCount is 0, which is under 50 at :605, and reconcileTombstones (:630-645) marks every saved non-curated preset as gone. (2) local- palettes: localPaletteToUnified (:712-730) gives isCurated:false and isFromAPI:false, and the Save button in preset-card.ts:428-434 is unconditional. The toggle at :877-878 accepts it, so a saved local palette is never in the `live` set and gets tombstoned on every load. That case is deterministic, not transient. (3) Stale query: handleSearchInput (:999-1005) updates searchQuery right away and has no sequence guard. A filtered response that lands after the query is cleared passes the `this.searchQuery` guard at :631. No test asserts markDeleted: preset-tool.test.ts:120 only mocks it. Severity stays MEDIUM, not HIGH. A tombstone is a reversible flag (saved-presets-service.ts:155-159) and no data is lost. keepDeleted defaults to true (:127), so by default the user sees a false "Removed by its author" chip rather than a missing preset. Triggers (1) and (3) need a failure or race while the page is open, and they clear on the next good load. Trigger (2) is permanent but only affects users who star their own palette. Recovery is weaker than the finding says: when a later page is full (apiCount >= 50) reconciliation is skipped (:605-611), so false tombstones can stick. The hybrid sort+slice (:321-326) can also cut API rows under the default 'popular' sort when community rows tie with curated rows at 0 votes. That would run reconciliation against a truncated page with no failure at all. Both points support at least MEDIUM, and neither is demonstrated well enough to raise it.
skeptic.evidence: apps/web-app/src/services/hybrid-preset-service.ts:128 (apiAvailable latched once), :315-317 (catch only warns, local list returned), :321-326 (sort then slice to limit). apps/web-app/src/services/community-preset-service.ts:276-283 (throws PresetApiError on !response.ok), :299 (timeout throws). apps/web-app/src/components/v4/preset-tool.ts:598 (offline = !isAPIAvailable()), :604-606 (apiCount < 50 -> reconcile), :631 (guard reads the current searchQuery, not the query that was fetched), :634-643 (every non-curated saved id missing from `live` gets markDeleted(true)), :712-725 (local- palette: isCurated false, isFromAPI false), :127 (keepDeleted: true by default), :803 (hidden only when keepDeleted is off), :999-1005 (no load sequence or stale-response guard). apps/web-app/src/components/v4/preset-card.ts:428-434 (Save button rendered for every card, including local-). apps/web-app/src/services/saved-presets-service.ts:155-159 (markDeleted only flips a flag, so it is reversible). apps/web-app/src/components/v4/__tests__/preset-tool.test.ts:120 (markDeleted mocked, never asserted, so the behaviour is untested). I wrote no repro file; every step of the path above is a direct read of the code.

skeptic.reason: I could not refute the defect, but I would grade it LOW, not MEDIUM. Each claim checks out in the code. getAffectedCommands (apps/discord-worker/src/services/preferences.ts:633-660) maps blending to /mixer and /gradient, matching to /swatch, and clan/gender to /swatch. The /preferences set handler (apps/discord-worker/src/handlers/commands/preferences.ts:375, rendered at about :421) puts those strings into the success embed. In practice gradient.ts:39-40 takes color_space from its own option, defaulting to 'hsv', and never reads prefs.blending. resolveBlendingMode is called only at mixer-v4.ts:68. swatch.ts:61 reads only prefs.theme, and SwatchInput gets its data from the .chara file. Outside the writer, nothing reads prefs.clan or prefs.gender. harmony.ts:80 does call resolveMatchingMethod, but harmony is missing from the matching list. The origin is MAIN, and the dead-code audit does not cover this, so it is not a duplicate. Why LOW: every command still produces correct output for its own inputs. The defect is the confirmation embed and the option descriptions (schemas.ts:674,681; en.json:1139,1142) claiming effects that never happen, plus clan/gender settings that do nothing. That is misleading text, which the brief's scale calls cosmetic (LOW). It is not a wrong result on a computation path (MEDIUM).
skeptic.evidence: I grepped apps/discord-worker/src and packages/bot-logic/src, excluding tests. prefs.clan and prefs.gender are written only at services/preferences.ts:194,197 and read nowhere. In packages/bot-logic, the only `gender` reads are character.gender from the parsed .chara (swatch.ts:247, glamour.ts:263). resolveBlendingMode is called only at mixer-v4.ts:68. resolveMatchingMethod is called from extractor.ts:233,461, gradient.ts:83, harmony.ts:80 and mixer-v4.ts:69, so harmony reads matching but is left out of the list. Budget reads prefs.matching directly at budget.ts:189,527. The tests do not catch this; they lock in the wrong mapping. preferences.test.ts:470-475 asserts that blending contains '/gradient' and clan contains '/swatch'. preferences.exhaustive.test.ts:424-434 asserts clan/gender map to '/swatch', and its other cases only check that the list is non-empty. No test compares the mapping against the handlers that actually read each key. I did not need a repro test; the static path is unambiguous.
